successors.name: State of Eritrea
successors.text: Eritrea: "allowing the EPLF fighters to enter the city on May 24" (1991); independence by referendum in April 1993

ledger.x: 1 September 1961: the Eritrean armed struggle begins at the Battle of Adal.
1975-1977: the fronts liberate nearly all of Eritrea.
1978: the Derg counter-offensive forces the EPLF back to Nakfa.

May 1991: the rebels win and hold Eritrea de facto; "In April 1993, the Eritrean people voted almost unanimously in favour of independence" and the United Nations admitted Eritrea on 28 May 1993; the Third Congress in 1994 turned the front into a political movement.

wars.name: Eritrean War of Independence
wars.outcome: EPLF victory: Afabet 1988, Massawa 1990, Asmara on 24 May 1991; independence confirmed by the April 1993 referendum.

wars.name: ELF-EPLF civil wars
wars.outcome: The ELF declared war on the EPLF in mid-1972 and the first civil war ended without a clear winner in 1974; the fronts reconciled in 1975; clashes resumed (August 1980) and most ELF fighters retreated into Sudan by 1981.

wars.name: Derg counter-offensive of 1978
wars.outcome: Saturation bombing from May 1978 and a ground offensive from July 1978 forced a strategic withdrawal to the Nakfa line, which held in the January-February 1979 offensive.

certainty.note: Guerrilla zones and front lines, never a fixed border; the 1977 liberated area is defined by four towns kept by the Ethiopian army.
